title: Scheduled tasks / cron
overview: Review a synthetic cron modification and compare a user-managed schedule with approved deployment automation.
prerequisites: Read the baseline and compare event fields. No external tools are required.

attack.name: Cron
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: A root-owned cron change originating from an interactive write is worth checking against change management.
evidence: Find the writer, schedule owner, file path and change window. Compare the review record for the host.
false_positive: An administrator may create a job during approved maintenance.
tuning: Join known deployment identities and documented change windows. Keep unexpected schedule owners visible.
response: Preserve the audit trail and job definition, verify the owner, then remove an unauthorized entry according to policy.
prevention: Restrict cron directory writes and monitor job definitions and changes.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The Linux case exercises cron. Scheduled Task on Windows requires a different sensor and field map.

questions.explanation: The schedule owner and the actor are distinct fields.

options: A verified maintenance record with matching scope
questions.explanation: Authorization requires a change record, accountable actor and matching host.
